name: Sweet and sour pork stir-fry
summary: Lean pork strips stir-fried with peppers, carrot and fresh pineapple in a tangy tomato and pineapple sauce with no added sugar, over brown rice.
about: Sweet and sour pork comes from Cantonese cooking, where the pork is battered and deep-fried before it meets the sauce. This version stir-fries lean pork fillet instead and sweetens the sauce with pineapple and its juice rather than sugar.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.note: medium; peeled, cored and cut into bite-sized chunks

steps: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil over high heat. Add the brown rice and boil, uncovered, for 25–30 minutes, until tender but still a little chewy. Drain well, return it to the pot and cover to keep warm.
While the rice cooks, prepare the pineapple. Stir the pineapple juice, tomato paste, vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp cornflour and water together in a jug until smooth.
Slice the pork into thin strips, about 5 mm thick, and toss with the 2 tsp soy sauce and 2 tsp cornflour.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat until it shimmers. Stir-fry the pork in two batches for 2–3 minutes each, until browned and no longer pink inside. Tip onto a plate.

Add the rest of the oil, the onion and carrot and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the onion starts to soften. Add both peppers, the garlic and the ginger and stir-fry for 2 minutes more; the peppers should still be crisp.
Add the pineapple and stir-fry for 1 minute to warm it. Stir the sauce, pour it in and let it bubble for 1–2 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Return the pork and its juices and toss for 1 minute, until hot through. Spoon it over the brown rice and finish with the spring onions.
prepNote: Cut the pork, pineapple and vegetables and mix the sauce up to a day ahead; keep them covered in the fridge.
